holidays.name: Winnie the Pooh Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the honey-loving bear from the Hundred Acre Wood. Share a pot of honey, reread a favorite story, or practice Pooh-style kindness and gentle naps.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of A. A. Milne, born January 18, 1882, who created Winnie-the-Pooh and based the stories on his son Christopher Robin's stuffed animals.
holidays.funFact: Pooh was partly inspired by a real black bear named Winnipeg, who lived at the London Zoo and was brought to England by a Canadian soldier.

holidays.name: National Thesaurus Day
holidays.description: A word-nerd holiday for finding better, fancier, or funnier ways to say what you mean. Swap out a tired word for a more vivid one and enjoy the vocabulary.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of Peter Mark Roget, born January 18, 1779, who published his famous thesaurus in 1852.
holidays.funFact: Roget was a physician and inventor, and he began his word lists as a hobby long before they became one of the world's best-known reference books.

holidays.name: National Peking Duck Day
holidays.description: A salute to the glossy, crisp-skinned roasted duck, served with thin pancakes, scallions, and sweet bean sauce. It's a good excuse for a fancy dinner.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors a dish that dates back centuries in Chinese cuisine.
holidays.funFact: Traditional Peking duck is often carved at the table, and a skilled chef may slice it into more than 100 pieces.
